q: How do I calculate CO2 from gasifying petroleum coke into syngas?
title: Petcoke gasification: CO2 by mass balance
short: Work from carbon. Every tonne of carbon in the petcoke that leaves as CO2, whether from burning the syngas or from the shift step that makes hydrogen, is 3.67 tonnes of CO2. Petcoke is mostly carbon, so a lab analysis of your lots and the tonnes fed give the figure; subtract only carbon that leaves in products.
audience: Refineries, fertiliser and chemical plants that gasify petroleum coke for fuel gas, hydrogen or chemicals

ul: Tonnes of petcoke fed x carbon content from your lab report = tonnes of carbon in.
Subtract carbon that leaves in products such as methanol or captured CO2 sold under contract.
Carbon left x 44/12 = tonnes of CO2 emitted.

p: If the syngas is burnt for heat or power, the CO2 leaves the stack. If it is shifted to make hydrogen, a concentrated CO2 stream comes out of the shift and acid gas removal. Both count unless the CO2 is permanently stored or sold into a product with evidence.

sections.h: Default if you have no lab data
p: The IPCC 2006 default for petroleum coke is 97.5 kg CO2 per GJ at about 32.5 GJ per tonne, which is about 3.17 tonnes of CO2 per tonne. Use it only as a labelled fallback.

example.title: Worked example: one day of feed
lines: 1,000 t petcoke at 87% carbon = 870 t carbon
Less 20 t carbon leaving in a chemical product = 850 t carbon
example.note: Carbon content is an assumption for illustration; use your own lab results.
